newsitem.title: HUNGARY: DAIWA EUROPE SEES HUNGARY STOCKS CONTINUING UPTREND.
newsitem.headline: DAIWA EUROPE SEES HUNGARY STOCKS CONTINUING UPTREND.

text.p: Hungarian stocks should continue their upward climb in 1997, with the Budapest stock exchange's BUX index targeted to hit 6,500 by year's end, Daiwa Europe Limited said in a research report.
"Hungary's fundamental strength lies in its earnings, and we believe earnings performance for 1996 represents a sustainable trend," Daiwa Europe said in its March "Equity Strategy Quarterly".
"In fact Hungary, alone among all European markets, has seen its market consensus earnings estimates for 1996 rise by 10 percent from January to January," the report said.
The report said that more portfolio funds should move into the region and Hungary, which had one of the world's best performing stock markets last year, would be "one of the first beneficiaries".
It rated Hungary just behind Russia for investment potential, and ahead of Poland, Prague and Slovakia.
"We are therefore maintaining our recommended regional overweighting relative to regional market capitalisation (15 percent versus an actual six percent)," Daiwa said.
"Our year-end target for the BUX Index is 6,500, which would bring the market to a PER of 14.4X for 1997, but a more reasonable (and much more relevant) 11.4x for 1998."
The report said Daiwa analysts continue to recommend plastics maker Graboplast and meat processor Pick Szeged, largely because of export growth potential.
It said energy company MOL Rt, which represents just under 25 percent of the bourse's capitalisation, is "fundamentally undervalued despite delays in freeing regulated energy prices".
It said bank shares maintain their value despite recent strength and picks spirits maker Zwack Unicum as likely to benefit from export growth and recovery of the domestic economy.
The report says that it has downgraded hotels company Danubius to sell from buy because price appreciation from its plan to acquire Hungaria Hotels "has pushed its valuation to unsustainable levels".
"Also on the sell side we have foods company Globus which appears poorly placed to maintain its margins on weak export performance and a slow home market for its products."
